# DSH Session Toolkit
Adds two buttons to the DSH conversation header:
| Button | What it does |
| ⇄ Workspace | Moves the current session into another registered workspace (optionally archiving th

e original) |
| ◈ Preset | Switches the Agent preset of the current session — **including sessions t
hat already started** |
Both are things a browser half cannot do alone, which is why this plugin ships a host half as well.
## Install

Then restart `dsh web`.
## Why a host half is required
**Workspace membership is derived, not stored.** A session belongs to a workspace because the `cwd`

in
its `session header` equals the workspace path — `dsh-workspace`'s `sessionIds` getter filters on

that
condition every time, and `attachSession` refuses a session whose cwd does not match. The head

er is
immutable and no API rewrites `cwd`, so "moving" a session means **opening a continuation sess

ion in the
target directory that carries the whole history**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The new session keeps fork provenance (`parentSession`, `isSeeded`, the `session/end-seed` marker),
because the harness has no "delete session" and no "change session id". It also starts on the model

the
source last used — read from the last `model/selection` event, or, when the picker was never tou

ched,
from the `config` of the last `request/header` event — because the persona prefix's `{{model}}

` variable
only resolves from the options the Agent was created with.
**`agentPresets.select` only accepts a blank session.** It throws `agent-preset/locked` once the ses

sion
has run a turn. The plugin tries that official path first, and only when it is refused does it

rebind the
same Agent scope through `agentPresets.recompose(agent.ctx, id)` and write the `agent-pre

set/selected`
event that call would have written. History is not rewritten; projections and browser

`
event that call would have written. History is not rewritten; projections and browser tabs follow.
## Channels

The browser half calls two host routes of this package with relative-URL `fetch` (deliberately not
s
ession commands, so nothing lands in the session log as `command/run`):

- `POST /session-toolkit/migrate` — `{ sessionId, workspaceId, archiveSource?, agentPreset? }`
- `PO
ST /session-toolkit/preset` — `{ sessionId, agentPreset }`

Both pass `connection.requestRejection` (login cookie / loopback / same-site checks) first, accept
`
application/json` only, and cap the body at 64 KiB.
## Known limits
- A migration produces a **new session id**; the original history is untouched. To get it back, unar

chive
the source session in its original workspace.
- Switching the preset changes the system prompt

and tool catalog of the next request, so the provider's
prefix cache is invalidated from the first

token. While a turn is running the route answers
`session-busy`.
- Switching the preset does not swi
tch the model: model choice belongs to the session, not to the preset.
